about: Two lists of US common stocks on Nasdaq, the NYSE, and NYSE American. ETFs, ETNs, warrants, units, rights, preferreds, and test issues are left out, as are names under $3 or under $2 million of average daily dollar volume. The research list is the wide oversold screen: a low RSI, a lower Bollinger touch, or a pullback. A swing candidate is separate and smaller. It has to clear hard gates: no single session down about 9% or more in the last 8 sessions (still being above the 200-day does not waive that), no earnings inside 7 days, average daily dollar volume of at least $20 million, a rising 200-day average with the close at least 5% above it, a 21-session pullback that is not a 15% or worse slide, volume confirmation, at least two reversal signals, a swing score of at least 36, and reward-to-risk of at least 2:1 measured from the planned entry. The entry is a limit at structure under the close, or a next-session reclaim of the signal high. It is not today's close. After a shock bar the plan is skipped, so a pre-crash 20-day average is not reused as a target and a gap-inflated ATR is not the stop. The headline rank and the journal use the swing score only. Fundamentals are notes on the card and do not promote a name. The journal does not fill leftover slots with names that failed the gates, keeps one name per sector, and records no new official picks when SPY is under its 200-day. RSI is Wilder's 14-day RSI. Bollinger Bands are the 20-day average plus and minus two population standard deviations. ATR is Wilder's 14-day average true range, with the stop distance capped so one wide bar cannot set it. Yahoo quoteSummary is tried first. If that crumb is blocked, Nasdaq's public quote, annual financials, analyst target, and earnings calendar are used instead. Every sentence uses a fetched number. This is a rules screen, not a guarantee and not financial advice. fetchedAt is when this file was last filled. A failed fetch keeps the previous rows.
disclaimer: Informational only, not financial advice and not a recommendation to buy or sell. A stock is listed because it matched a rules-based swing screen.
source: Yahoo Finance public daily chart API (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart). Fundamentals come from Yahoo quoteSummary (summaryProfile, summaryDetail, financialData, defaultKeyStatistics, calendarEvents) when the public crumb is available, otherwise from Nasdaq's public quote, financials, analyst target, ratings, and earnings calendar (https://api.nasdaq.com/).
